Flexible Cards - Numbers - Full-Width (Global)
Numbers (Global | h2 used above h3)
Myth
#1
If I have more than one RRSP, my bank will tell me if I’m over-contributing
Each financial institution can only track your contributions towards the plan held there. Contact the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) with questions about your contribution room.
Myth
#2
I’m happy with my contribution amount, so no need to talk to a professional
There’s more to a review than your contribution amount. Things like your risk level, needs and goals should be reviewed regularly to ensure your money is invested properly depending on how far you are from retirement.
Myth
#3
Only an RRSP can help me save for retirement
Did you know that taking advantage of saving in a TFSA now could save you money when it’s time to withdraw the funds in retirement? Remember, withdrawals from TFSAs are not taxable. RRSP withdrawals are.

Update your budget
Now is a great time to revisit your My Money budget and re-evaluate how much money comes in and where it goes. Look for costs to cut back this month and put that extra money towards your debt.
Use cash
Credit cards are convenient, I know. But if you’re actively working on reducing your debt, don’t add to your balances. Using cash will help you separate your needs and wants.
Know the signs
If the amount you owe is keeping you up at night, or you simply have no idea where to start, we’re here to help. Contact a Retirement Counselor for personalized guidance.
